gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: It’s a public seafront and the prom is flat and paved, so a pushchair is fine. It gets packed near the Tower in the afternoon, so I would find your spot early.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: From May to September dogs aren’t allowed on the beach between North Pier and the Mirror Ball, and they must be on a lead on the prom between North and South Piers. The jets are loud, so I would think carefully before bringing yours.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: Bring a picnic if you like. Drinking alcohol in public is banned on the promenade and it can be taken off you, and glass isn’t allowed on the beach or the sea wall.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: Folding chairs and blankets are fine. I couldn’t find a rule on gazebos or windbreaks for the show, so I would ask before you take anything big, as space by the sea wall gets tight.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: I couldn’t find any refill points for the show. There’s almost no shade on the prom, so I would bring more water than you think you’ll need, in plastic bottles.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: There’s a council Changing Places toilet at the Holiday Inn on Talbot Gateway, open 08:00 to 20:00 in summer and about 10 minutes’ walk from the front. The prom toilets have accessible loos on a RADAR key.

gtk.title: Carers' tickets
gtk.text: The show is free for everyone, so there’s no carer ticket to sort out. You just turn up.

gtk.title: Hearing support
gtk.text: I couldn’t find anything on hearing loops or BSL for the show. I would ask Visit Blackpool before you go if you need support.

gtk.title: Quiet area
gtk.text: I couldn’t find a calm or sensory space for the show. If someone needs a break from the noise, the streets back from the front are much quieter than the prom.

gtk.title: Re-entry
gtk.text: It’s an open public seafront with no gates, so you can wander off into town and come back whenever you like.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: There are event first aiders, and any steward or police officer can point you to them. I couldn’t find a lost children point for 2026, so I would agree a meeting point like the Tower and put your number on younger ones.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. It’s a two day show, so if one day looks poor the other may be better.

ground.html:
The Ground Show

There’s no airfield at Blackpool, so the ground show is the Air Show Village on the Tower Festival Headland, with the whole resort wrapped round it. In 2026 the village opened at 11:00 and the flying didn’t start until about 14:00. That gives you a good few hours. I would use them well, before the prom gets properly packed.

WhereTower Festival Headland
Open11:00 to 18:00 (2026)
CostFree to walk round
FlyingFrom about 14:00 (2026)

Things To See

Free

Meet The Armed Forces

You can meet aircraft ground crews and serving members of the armed forces, hear about their roles and get up close to some of the kit they use. If anyone in your group is thinking of joining, I would suggest bringing your questions.

Free

A Jet On The Ground

At a past show there was a Typhoon in the village that you could get right up to, with a look into the cockpit. I couldn’t confirm one for 2026, so treat it as a bonus if it turns up. If an aircraft is opened up for a look inside, keep an eye out for exclusive merch in or outside it.

Free

Activities For Children

There are interactive stands and things for children to do, and kids love to see the forces stands. The sand right in front of the display helps too. More ideas in .

Varies

Trader Stalls

A long run of stalls and attractions lines the prom through the village. I would have a look round before the crowds arrive, as it gets hard to browse once the flying is close.

Varies

Food In The Village

The village has its own food concessions, and the town behind you has hundreds more. My notes on eating, toilets and access are in .

How I Would Do It

  1. Save your pitch firstIf you want a front row seat by the sea wall, head there first and set up your chairs or blanket. Then one of you can go and explore. Have a look at if you’re unsure.
  2. Walk the village before 14:00Speak to the crews, visit the trade stalls and check the food options while it’s still quiet enough to move.
  3. Toilet before the flyingI would go before the flying starts, as the Undercroft toilets by North Pier get very busy.
  4. Use the gapsIf you aren’t waiting for a particular display, use it as a toilet or food break. That’s when I nip back to the village.
Jack’s tipDon’t rush off when the last display ends. The village stayed open until 18:00 in 2026, and a wander round it beats sitting in a queue for the M55.
Air Show VillageWhat’s on in the village this year

Times and stands may change for 2027.

skipped.flights: I couldn't find any pleasure, helicopter or warbird flights offered at or from the show on the promenade. Blackpool Airport has general helicopter experiences, but nothing tied to the air show that I could confirm.
skipped.support: Blackpool Council funds the show and I found no air show donation, programme sale, bucket collection or volunteer appeal. The Visit Blackpool donate page is for the Illuminations only.

notes: 1) Village hours conflict on the official site: the 2026 news piece (8 July 2026) says 11:00 to 18:00, but the Air Show Village page still says 12:00 to 19:00 and mentions a Typhoon you could look into the cockpit of. That page looks out of date, so I used 11:00 to 18:00 and called the Typhoon a past show. https://www.visitblackpool.com/latest-news/one-month-to-go-until-blackpool-air-show-returns/ and https://www.visitblackpool.com/things-to-do/events/blackpool-air-show/village/ 2) The page says 'Static aircraft: None' in the Right for you table; that matches 2026 as far as I can tell, but if a Typhoon returns to the village it would need changing. 3) The page (Help and Facilities) says there's a Changing Places toilet at Blackpool Tower. I couldn't confirm that today. The council toilet list names the Holiday Inn (Talbot Gateway) and Solaris Centre/Harrowside Changing Places only: https://www.blackpool.gov.uk/Residents/Planning-environment-and-community/Public-toilets.aspx 4) The alcohol rule is from the Town Centre and Promenade PSPO (renewed 2024), which also bans overnight tents and glass on the beach and sea wall: https://www.blackpool.gov.uk/Residents/Planning-environment-and-community/Crime-and-safety/Public-space-protection-orders/Town-centre-and-promenade.aspx
